\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
"$\pm$ 0": std below 1e-08 of the mean (numerical noise; fixed test set and deterministic fit), not exactly zero.\par
SymGWR-T = degree-5 polynomial + k=1 nearest-reference Taylor surrogate (\texttt{SymGWR} in the CSVs); SymGWR-R = residual-anchored variant (\texttt{residual\_anchored}, from taylor\_variants\_accuracy\_per\_seed.csv).\par
SymGWR-R-IDW / SymGWR-R-CS (k=4) = residual-anchored polynomial plus an inverse-distance / compactly supported blend of the k nearest reference residuals (ridwcs\_accuracy\_per\_seed.csv); the cubic row is a cubic interpolant along T (random, temp.-band) or along the composition arm (comp.-group) through the reference rows (interp\_baselines\_per\_seed.csv).\par
(i) Random: 10 random 60/20/20 resamples; test sets overlap, pairs not strictly independent\par
(ii) Temp.-band: test set fixed (1,568 rows, same for every seed); only train/val partition varies\par
(iii) Comp.-group: 5 folds x 2 shuffles: test fold = seed \% 5, so 5 distinct test sets, each seen twice\par
(a) Comp.-group: cubic along the composition arm is defined for only 81\% of the test rows (composition bracketed by reference compositions on its arm; star-centre and out-of-range rows have no value). Its metrics are on those rows only, where SymGWR-T has MAPE 0.0434\% (all rows: 0.0630\%); it is therefore excluded from the bold best-of ranking in this split.\par
(b) train rows capped at 2500 (random subsample, seed-dependent); val rows added on refit\par
(c) temperature column moved to index 0 before train\_pinn: the library physics loss penalises dG/d(feature 0), and feature 0 in the data is Mass\_fraction\_Nb\par
(d) GP protocol: alpha tuned on a 1000-row train subsample (val MSE), then ONE refit on train (capped 2500) + val; 25 min timeout\par
Seeds per method: 10; timeouts: 0, errors: 0.\par
\end{minipage}

\par\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
SymGWR-T extrapolates linearly from the nearest reference, so value and gradient both jump at cell boundaries. SymGWR-R adds a constant offset to the polynomial P, so its gradient (grad P) is continuous (jumps are zero up to rounding) and only the value jumps.\par
SymGWR-R-IDW / -CS blend the residuals of the k=4 nearest references. Event: NN switch = the nearest reference changes; k-set = the set of the k nearest references changes (k-th and (k+1)-th reference swap); support (CS only) = the (k+1)-th reference changes with the k-set unchanged, which moves the support radius. The NN-switch rows of the blended variants are the same event type as the SymGWR-T and SymGWR-R rows.\par
Events = reference-change events located by bisection and evaluated on both sides, summed over seeds; tie-plane events excluded: 0. SymGWR-T/R and the blended variants use independently drawn segments, so event counts differ between them. For the blended variants at most 5,000 events per split and seed are evaluated (random subsample; 50,000 = capped in all 10 seeds).\par
\end{minipage}

Slope: least-squares fit of log query time on log n over 12 points = 4 distinct sizes $\times$ 3 repeats, so the CI rests on only 4 distinct sizes. Every CI excludes 0 (time grows with n for every method; slope $<$ 1 is sublinear).\par

Caveat: the pycalphad database is a steel database (mc\_fe\_v2.059.pycalphad.tdb, Fe--Cr--Ni--C--Mn--Mo--Si), not the Nb--Al--Ti--Mo--Fe--Ni--Cr system SymGWR is fitted to, and pycalphad was timed in a separate run (calphad\_reference\_timing\_pycalphad*.csv), not under the pinned-core protocol above; the ratios indicate orders of magnitude only.\par
